summary: A 1931 steel tower raised for J.K. Lilly near Nashville, Indiana, later given to Indiana University; sources disagree on whether it was moved and whether it can be climbed.

facts.design: 75-foot steel tower with a 7x7 steel cab and wooden steps (register)
facts.agency: Indiana University Research and Teaching Preserve

access.note: Register: access by permission only. Indiana Fire Towers: not publicly accessible. The Outbound says a park tower is open to climb; sources disagree.

events.note: Erected for J.K. Lilly at his expense, per the 1931 newspaper and the 1932 state report; the register gives 1930
Land donated to Indiana University by the Lilly family

corrections.why: A 1931 newspaper and the 1932 state report both say the tower was erected in 1931. The register's 1930 build field is the only source for that year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1930 and says the CCC built it in the 1930s. The 1931 newspaper and the 1932 state report say J.K. Lilly paid to have it erected in 1931.
The register and The Outbound say 75 feet; the 1931 newspaper planned 80 feet. The story uses the register's 75 feet.

Not resolved. The Outbound says the tower was moved to Brown County State Park and is open for the public to climb. Indiana Fire Towers and the register place it on Indiana University land with no public access.

sources.title: Lilly - FOREST LOOKOUTS
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (easternuslookouts.weebly.com), quoting the Brown County Democrat, April 1931

sources.title: Climb Lilly Lookout at Brown County State Park

notes_for_editor: Location and access disputed: The Outbound says the tower was moved to Brown County State Park and can be climbed; Indiana Fire Towers and the register say it stands on IU land with no public access. The story does not encourage climbing. Build year (1930 register vs 1931 contemporary sources) and height (75 vs 80 ft) also disputed. Nothing found on staffing or notable fires.
